goals.primaryObjective: Generate 150 qualified pipeline opportunities from 500 customer and prospect attendees, and give the platform team a public roadmap moment.
objectives: Recruit 10 customers willing to be named references or case studies
Drive 40% of attendees into a hands-on product workshop
Give regional sales 25 pre-booked executive meetings on site
goals.businessJustification: Renewals in the enterprise segment slipped 6 points last year, and win/loss interviews point to weak awareness of the platform roadmap among existing accounts. A single flagship in-person moment is the cheapest way to reach the top 200 accounts with both product depth and executive access before the FY27 planning cycle.

audience.description: Existing enterprise customers and late-stage prospects across North America — platform practitioners plus the executive sponsors who own their budget. Roughly 70% customer, 30% prospect.

targetPersonas.name: Practitioner attendee
targetPersonas.title: Platform Engineering Manager
targetPersonas.description: Runs the day-to-day implementation. Comes for hands-on sessions, migration guidance and peer conversations; strongly influences renewal but does not sign.
painPoints: Needs concrete migration guidance, not a product pitch
Has to justify two days away from an on-call rotation

targetPersonas.name: Executive sponsor
targetPersonas.title: VP Engineering / CTO
targetPersonas.description: Attends the keynote and the executive track. Cares about roadmap credibility, benchmarks and peer conversation.
painPoints: Limited time on site — will skip anything that feels like a demo
Wants evidence of business outcomes from comparable companies

allocations.notes: Moscone West, two days including move-in
Breakfast, lunch and one evening reception
Main stage plus three breakout rooms
Paid social, email and field outreach

budget.notes: High-level only — vendor-level detail and commitments are tracked in the Budget Builder. 8% contingency is held centrally and is not shown here.

venueOrPlatform.name: Moscone West
venueOrPlatform.notes: Level 2 for the main stage, Level 3 for breakouts and the sponsor lounge.

successMetrics.notes: Total confirmed registrations by event day

riskRegister.risk: Registrations exceed venue capacity, or fall so far short the room looks empty
riskRegister.mitigation: Hard cap registration at 540 (90% of fire-code capacity) and review pacing weekly from 8 weeks out; hold a waitlist.

riskRegister.risk: Keynote speaker cancels close to the event
riskRegister.mitigation: Confirm speakers in writing by 14 Aug, keep two vetted backups warm, and pre-record a fallback session by 20 Oct.

riskRegister.risk: Registration falls short of target because promotion starts too late
riskRegister.mitigation: Lock the promo calendar before registration opens; mid-campaign checkpoint at 50% of target with $8k paid budget in reserve.

riskRegister.risk: AV or production failure during a main-stage session
riskRegister.mitigation: Full technical rehearsal on 11 Nov, redundant mics and laptops on site, named AV vendor contact on the run of show.
Base the guarantee on a 72% historical check-in rate and confirm the final count on 29 Oct.

milestones.label: Agenda published and promotion campaign live
Final headcount and catering guarantee to venue
Run of show finalised and AV rehearsal complete
Leads handed off to sales with follow-up owners
Retro complete and ROI report published

items: Executive sponsor is only on site for the morning of day one
No budget for a second evening event — reception is the only social moment
Registration data must stay in the US region for enterprise customer contracts
Book the AV vendor 90 days out — 60 was too late last year
constraints.notes: Two competitor conferences fall in the same month; the date is fixed by the executive calendar and cannot move.

carryForwardLessons.lesson: Book the AV vendor 90 days out — 60 was too late and cost us the preferred rate.
Breakout rooms sized on registration interest, not room availability — two sessions turned people away last year.
